newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour says elderly insurance a small step.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour says elderly insurance a small step.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party said proposals by the Conservative government to offer private insurance for residential care for the elderly were no more than a small step towards dealing with a major problem.

"It's a small step, a partial answer," shadow health secretary Chris Smith told BBC Radio Four. "The government's scheme is of some benefit to some people and as such is something that's obviously welcome. But it's a limited number of people that it is going to benefit."
Smith said that old people who wanted to protect the full value of their homes would need cash of up to 10,000 stg to buy a policy to protect their assets.
"There is a very small number of pensioners who are actually in a position to be able to do that," he said.

The government proposal did not measure up to the overall challenge and there were many other things that needed to be done, such as ensuring uniform national care guidelines. "We would want to put those in place," Smith said.
